The argument given for a limit of \(1/r!\) does not hold up.  
For \(r=1\) the forbidden configuration \(\{n,p_1n\}\) forces any maximal subset of the powers of a single prime to have asymptotic density \(1/2\); the proposed formula would give \(1\), which is clearly false.  
A natural construction that avoids the forbidden “star’’ for general \(r\) is to keep all smooth numbers whose total exponent sum is congruent to a fixed residue modulo \(r+1\). This yields a density of \(1/(r+1)\), and standard extremal‑combinatorial arguments show that this density is optimal. Hence the correct limit is \(1/(r+1)\), not \(1/r!\).

**Verdict:** REJECT.
